title: MZ Wildsilver — now in Early Access!

posts.author: Saireau
posts.body:
Early Access
Wildsilver
is the fifth JRPG created by Great Potion Games. This is the early-access version of the game, 0.9.x. It contains the complete story, all skills, items, equipment, enemies, locations et cetera.
It's a
full gaming experience
, but there will be
regular patches with improvements
.
Version 1.0.0 will be released once I feel like development is practically done and there are no 'should-dos' anymore. A piece of art is never finished, only abandoned, but this will be the point where I don't make changes proactively anymore (while still reacting to feedback). Version 0.9.x is priced at 4,99 USD, while version 1.0.x will be 9,99 USD.
https://great-potion-games.itch.io/wildsilver
Story
Accompany Velven on a mission to save her sister Soire who has been poisoned by a Basilisk. Meet a little robot with a hammer and a brave knight from the capital who offer their help and venture right into the lair of the fierce dragon.
From there, the story takes a few turns to become god-slayingly epic as expected from a game of this genre. You will acually get to see the capital yourself, find out what ancient secrets it hides and, though courage, skill and, to be fair, some lucky circumstances, save the world from destruction.
Gameplay
Explore environments, find chests, fight monsters, get stronger, learn skills, buy items, customise equipment, solve puzzles, talk to people, break urns. In that order if played as designed.
Features
15 hours of playtime
epic and emotional story
easy-going progression with some challenges
ATB system (you can choose between wait and active mode)
robotic companion (people seem to like Gilbert a lot)
many ways of accumulating power
many reversible customisation options (that is, equipment with effects)
finisher skills
clean level design and user interfaces
smooth lighting, tilt shift, parallax water and other visual effects
self-written soundtrack with 40+ tracks
awesome sound effect for critical hits (this is more important than you’d think!)
many cutscenes, but mainly short ones (I hope this is a good compromise)
British English
no time pressure (I didn’t like this in Majora’s Mask or Pikmin)
no missable items (no need to keep a guide and double-check every 5 minutes)
no game over (except for elite and boss battles)
Screenshots
Trailer
Get it now!
See more screenshots and download
Wildsilver
here:
https://great-potion-games.itch.io/wildsilver
Asset Creator?
Are you one of the talented people who have made assets used in
Wildsilver?
Send me a message! You'll get the game for free, of course!
If you have created assets that you think would fit this game phenomenally, please get in touch too!
Letsplayer? Streamer?
If you’re a letsplayer or streamer with a regular schedule that would have a slot for a session of
Wildsilver,
I'll gladly provide you with a key as well!
More Games
Please visit my website to find information about
Game Master, Game Master Plus, LV99: Final Fortress
and
Wildsilver Zero!
greatpotiongames.com
Have fun playing
and
please leave a review!

Um … I hadn't expected
this.
Well …
First of all: Wow, Nasciturus! I see you're really passionate about bugs in an early-access indie game — which can be a good thing!
I'm looking forward to the list of bugs you found, since I want to make this game the best experience it can be just as you do. I'm certainly not ignoring any bug reports on purpose while raking in all the money an RPG Maker game makes on Steam.

posts.author: Prajna
posts.body:
I have a hard time believing this statement. After making a post in a thread on Steam - which you did with regards to the bugs thread on your game's Steam forum -, you're automatically subbed to that thread, unless you manually unsub (afterwards). Seeing as this was the second time that a player of your commercially released game had to wait an inappropriate amount of time for your help with regards to a (potential) unavoidable game-breaking bug, you might want to check the message boards at least once daily - as every other (semi-)professional developer does. That shouldn't be so hard, considering that you're usually online on Steam all day.
If you can't or don't want to do that, that's okay, too, of course. Not everyone cares the same way about their games and players, not everyone can muster the same degree of dedication. It's all right to have other priorities, but that means your (potential) players will soon have other priorities, too. You want to be a successful human being, worker, maybe parent, and also game developer? I'm sorry, but you can't have it all, at least not with the mentality you've displayed so far.
Now the folks here will probably diss me again, since they're afraid they will be in your shoes sometime in the future (if they ever achieve to release a completed game commercially, which most of them won't manage to do), so you probably don't have to worry about anything. Attention spans, reading ability and rational thinking are practically nonexistent on the internet (and concerning humans in general), so you will continue to sell one digital copy of your game per month, and (negative) word of mouth won't spread. And next year at the latest, you won't have to worry about disappointing players anymore, because by then, there won't be any (potential) players left to disappoint.
By the way, you're wrong about this whole "angry folks and criticism means people care about the game" thing. They're simply angry, because your game and your service don't meet professional standards.

Basilisk: Lowered DEF by 10%.
Seraphim: Renamed to ‘Seraph’ (plural: ‘Seraphim’).
Behemoth: Raised ATK by 9%, lowered DEF by 10%.
Wyvern: Now uses Prepare, which is now required for Sinferno and Malizzard.
For enemies between Level 26 and 30, raised main stats by 1.
Commander’s Uniform: Now called Vanguard.
Taunt: Now handled as a buff.
Poison: Now degenerates HP by 5% (down from 20%) per turn left after battle.
Burn: Now degenerates HP by 5% (down from 10%), or 2% for elites and bosses (down from 4%).
Added an animation for taking damage from Poison after battle.
Revised every buff and debuff.
Manor: Roboguards now move as intended.
Swamp: Added a second Tanuki.
Polished Capital maps.
Reduced the intensity of the bloom lighting effect.
Weakness and resistance popups now work as intended.
Made many minor fixes and optimisations.
Updated plugins.
